title: Arc Length, Sector Area and Radians
seo_title: Sec 3 Arc length, sector area and radians Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
short_title: Arc length, sector area and radians
standard_text: arc length, sector area and area of a segment of a circle; use of radian measure of angle (including conversion between radians and degrees)
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on radian measure, converting between degrees and radians, arc length, sector area, segment area and perimeter of a sector. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: In radians, arc length s = rθ and sector area = ½r²θ.
key_sub: π radians = 180°. Segment area = sector area − triangle area.
body_html:
How it works

  • π radians = 180°. Degrees → radians: × π/180. Radians → degrees: × 180/π.
  • Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr (degrees) or s = rθ (radians).
  • Sector area = θ/360 × πr² (degrees) or ½r²θ (radians).
  • Segment area = sector area − triangle area = ½r²θ − ½r² sin θ.
Example

Convert 135° to radians.

135 × π ÷ 180

Answer: 3π/4

Example

A sector has radius 6 cm and angle 1.2 rad. Find its area and perimeter.

Area = ½ × 36 × 1.2 = 21.6 cm²

Arc = 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 cm, perimeter = 6 + 6 + 7.2

Answer: 21.6 cm² and 19.2 cm

Common mistakes

  • Using the radian formulas with an angle in degrees (or the other way round).
  • Using 2πr for an area or πr² for a length.
  • Forgetting the two radii when finding the perimeter of a sector.
  • Leaving the calculator in degree mode when working out sin θ for θ in radians.

faq.a: The angle at the centre of a circle when the arc length equals the radius. 2π radians make a full turn, so π radians = 180° and 1 radian ≈ 57.3°.

faq.q: What are the arc length and sector area formulas in radians?
faq.a: Arc length s = rθ and sector area = ½r²θ, where θ is in radians.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a segment?
faq.a: Subtract the area of the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord, ½r² sin θ, from the area of the sector.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a sector?
faq.a: Add the two radii to the arc length: 2r + rθ.
